name: Product ontology
purpose: Define product behavior, stakeholder requirements and optimization goals in a form that software factories can interpret consistently.

vocabulary.actors: Participants that own goals, take actions or supply authoritative evidence. People, organizations and software may participate.
vocabulary.entities: Things that keep their identity as their properties change.
vocabulary.relations: Directed associations between named actors or entities.
vocabulary.actions: Requests by an actor about a subject, with an explicit set of observable outcomes.
vocabulary.metrics: Measurements defined by unit, population, time window and evidence source.
vocabulary.requirements: Mandatory conditions with an accountable owner, stakeholder perspective and evidence check.
vocabulary.objectives: Directions of improvement used to compare eligible candidates.
vocabulary.scenarios: Concrete conditions and a trigger paired with an expected action outcome.

reference_semantics.path: A dot separates fields. An asterisk selects each object value or array element. Evaluate a path only where its fields are present.
reference_semantics.resolution: Each selected value must identify exactly one declaration of an allowed target kind.
reference_semantics.scenario_outcome: The expected outcome must occur in the outcomes of the scenario's referenced action.

perspectives.experience: What a participant can accomplish or observe.
perspectives.business: What an accountable operator requires or seeks to improve.

attestation_checks.applicability: Evidence must identify the assessment subject, named authority, claim and scope.

evaluation.evidence: Record the source, assessment subject and period. Distinguish test, projected and observed results. An operational claim requires observation for its declared period.
evaluation.eligibility: Every effective requirement must be satisfied. Preserve violated and unknown results separately.

ranking.when_present: Priority lists every effective objective exactly once.

evolution.evaluation: Compare agent interpretations on fixed inputs across versions. Record ontology version, agent version, inputs, expected decisions, observed decisions and clarification requests.
